city.name: Hyderabad
city.summary: City of Pearls and Nizams, where the Qutb Shahi legacy meets a modern skyline: Charminar, Golconda and a lakeside promenade.

place.name: Charminar
place.description: An iconic mosque-monument with four grand minarets, standing at the heart of the old city and serving as the visual symbol of Hyderabad.
place.history: Built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, to commemorate the end of a deadly plague in the city and to mark the founding of Hyderabad.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors through the day; the surrounding Laad Bazaar and Makkah Masjid can be explored on the same trip. Climbing to the upper floor offers a view over the old city.
place.bestTime: October to February, when the weather is cool and pleasant.
place.nearby: Laad Bazaar, Makkah Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace
place.tips: Visit early morning or evening to avoid crowds and heat; bargain for bangles and pearls in Laad Bazaar nearby.

place.name: Golconda Fort
place.description: A massive hilltop fortress that was once the capital of the Qutb Shahi kingdom and a global centre of diamond trade.
place.history: Originally a mud fort built by the Kakatiyas, it was rebuilt in granite by the Qutb Shahi rulers and later became famous for the Kohinoor and other legendary diamonds that passed through its markets.
place.visitingInfo: A guided walk through the fort covers palaces, armouries and the famous clapping point known for its acoustic design. A sound-and-light show is held in the evenings.
place.tips: Wear comfortable shoes for the climb and try the clapping point near the entrance to test the fort's famous acoustics.

place.name: Hussain Sagar Lake
place.description: A large heart-shaped artificial lake in the middle of the city, home to a striking monolithic statue of Buddha on a central island.
place.history: Built in 1563 by Hussain Shah Wali during the reign of Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah to supply water and connect the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad.
place.visitingInfo: Boat rides run through the day out to the Buddha statue; Tank Bund and Lumbini Park along the shore are popular for evening walks.
place.nearby: Lumbini Park, Necklace Road, Birla Mandir
place.tips: Evening boat rides offer pleasant views of the illuminated skyline around the lake.

place.name: Salar Jung Museum
place.description: One of the largest museums in India built almost entirely from a single family's private collection, spanning art and artifacts from across the world.
place.history: The collection was amassed by Salar Jung III, a former prime minister of Hyderabad state, and was later handed to the nation, becoming a museum of national importance.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Fridays; galleries cover sculpture, textiles, manuscripts, clocks and decorative art from India, Europe, the Middle East and the Far East.
place.bestTime: Year round, ideally in the cooler months of November to February.
place.nearby: Charminar, Chowmahalla Palace, Osmania General Hospital
place.tips: Don't miss the musical clock gallery, which draws a crowd right before the hour strikes.

place.name: Chowmahalla Palace
place.description: An elegant four-palace complex that served as the seat of the Nizams of Hyderabad, with grand courtyards and a vintage car collection.
place.history: Construction began under the Nizams in the 18th century and continued over decades, with the complex used for royal functions and to receive dignitaries.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Fridays; the Khilwat Mubarak durbar hall and the clock tower are highlights of the visit.
place.nearby: Charminar, Laad Bazaar, Salar Jung Museum
place.tips: Combine this with a Charminar visit since both are within walking distance of each other.

place.name: Ramoji Film City
place.description: One of the largest integrated film studio complexes in the world, open to visitors as a theme-park style attraction with film sets, gardens and live shows.
place.history: Founded by media entrepreneur Ramoji Rao in the 1990s, it has hosted the shooting of a very large number of Indian films in many languages.
place.visitingInfo: Guided studio tours cover film sets, gardens, stunt shows and rides. It lies outside the city, so plan a full-day outing.
place.tips: Start early and wear comfortable shoes, as the tour involves a lot of walking.

place.name: Birla Mandir
place.description: A white marble Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara on a hilltop above Hussain Sagar, with fine views over the city.
place.history: Built by the Birla Foundation over about a decade and consecrated in 1976, using white marble brought from Rajasthan.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors of all faiths; footwear must be removed and modest dress is expected.
place.nearby: Hussain Sagar Lake, Lumbini Park, Necklace Road
place.tips: Visit near sunset for views of the city lights, and avoid festival days if you prefer fewer crowds.

place.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
place.description: A quiet complex of large domed tombs of the Qutb Shahi rulers, set in landscaped gardens close to Golconda Fort.
place.history: The tombs were built over roughly two centuries as the resting places of the dynasty's rulers and their families.
place.visitingInfo: Visitors can walk among the granite and plasterwork tombs and the small mosque within the gardens.
place.tips: Combine with Golconda Fort, since the two are only a short drive apart.

place.name: Nehru Zoological Park
place.description: One of the largest zoos in India, with animals in spacious open enclosures and a lion safari.
place.history: Opened to the public in 1963 beside Mir Alam Tank.
place.visitingInfo: Battery-operated vehicles and a safari bus help visitors cover the large grounds; check the current visiting days before going.
place.nearby: Mir Alam Tank, Salar Jung Museum
place.tips: Carry water, wear comfortable shoes and use the park vehicles to save energy.

place.name: Mecca Masjid
place.location: Near Charminar, Old City, Hyderabad, Telangana
place.description: One of the oldest and largest mosques in India, with a vast prayer hall and tall arches beside Charminar.
place.history: Construction began in 1617 under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and was completed in 1694 under Mughal rule.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors with modest dress; visits should respect prayer times.
place.tips: Dress modestly and avoid the Friday midday congregation unless you are attending prayers.

city.name: Jaipur
city.summary: Rajasthan's royal capital, built around grand forts, jewel-box palaces and a centuries-old astronomical observatory.

place.name: Hawa Mahal
place.description: A pink sandstone palace with a honeycomb facade of 953 small windows, built so royal women could watch street life while remaining unseen.
place.history: Constructed in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, the five-storey facade was designed to resemble the crown of Lord Krishna.
place.visitingInfo: Best photographed from across the road in the morning light; the interior has a small museum and narrow ramps instead of stairs.
place.tips: Arrive early morning when the sun lights up the pink facade for the best photographs.

place.name: Amber Fort
place.description: A majestic hilltop fort-palace of pale yellow and pink sandstone overlooking Maota Lake, renowned for its mirrored halls.
place.history: Built by Raja Man Singh I, a Rajput general of Mughal emperor Akbar, and expanded by successive rulers over the following two centuries.
place.visitingInfo: Visitors can walk or take a jeep up to the fort; the Sheesh Mahal (mirror palace) and Ganesh Pol gate are highlights inside.
place.nearby: Jaigarh Fort, Maota Lake, Panna Meena ka Kund
place.tips: Go early to beat both the heat and the tour-bus crowds, and pair the visit with nearby Jaigarh Fort.

place.name: City Palace
place.description: A sprawling royal complex blending Rajput and Mughal architecture, still partly home to Jaipur's former royal family.
place.history: Construction began under Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the founder of Jaipur city, alongside the planning of the city itself in the early 18th century.
place.visitingInfo: The complex includes the Chandra Mahal, Mubarak Mahal and an armoury; certain private wings are open only with special-access tickets.
place.tips: Hire an audio guide or a local guide to appreciate the history behind each courtyard and gallery.

place.name: Jantar Mantar
place.description: A collection of large stone astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial, built for tracking celestial movements.
place.history: Constructed by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II between 1728 and 1734, it is one of five such observatories he built across northern India, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
place.visitingInfo: Guides on site can explain how each instrument was used to track time, seasons and planetary positions.
place.bestTime: October to March, around midday to see sundials in action.
place.tips: Visit around noon to see the massive sundial cast a clear, readable shadow.

place.name: Jal Mahal
place.description: A serene palace that appears to float on Man Sagar Lake, with four of its five floors submerged underwater.
place.history: Built in the 18th century, it was later renovated by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II and used as a lodge for royal duck-hunting parties.
place.visitingInfo: The interior is not open to the public, but the lakefront promenade offers excellent views and photo opportunities, especially at sunset.
place.bestTime: Evenings, year round, best in the cooler months.
place.tips: Visit at sunset when the palace and surrounding Aravalli hills are beautifully lit.

place.name: Nahargarh Fort
place.description: A hilltop fort on the Aravalli ridge, known for sweeping views over Jaipur, especially at sunset.
place.history: Built in 1734 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II as part of the city's defences.
place.visitingInfo: The ramparts, courtyards and pavilions offer panoramic views of the Pink City.
place.tips: Go in the late afternoon to watch the sun set over the city.

place.name: Jaigarh Fort
place.description: A rugged hill fort above Amber Fort, famous for its massive ramparts and the Jaivana cannon, one of the largest cannons on wheels in the world.
place.history: Built by Sawai Jai Singh II in the early 18th century to protect Amber Fort and its palace complex.
place.visitingInfo: Linked to Amber Fort by a fortified passage; inside are palaces, a small museum and large water-storage structures.
place.nearby: Amber Fort, Nahargarh Fort, Maota Lake
place.tips: Visit after Amber Fort and carry water, as there is little shade on the ramparts.

place.name: Albert Hall Museum
place.description: The oldest museum in Rajasthan, set in a striking Indo-Saracenic building with galleries of art, textiles, carpets and an Egyptian mummy.
place.history: Designed by Samuel Swinton Jacob, its foundation was laid in 1876 and it opened as a museum in 1887.
place.visitingInfo: Galleries show decorative arts, miniature paintings and weapons; the building is beautifully lit after dark.
place.nearby: Ram Niwas Garden, Hawa Mahal, City Palace
place.tips: Visit in the evening to see the building illuminated.

place.name: Galtaji Temple
place.description: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage complex of temples, pavilions and natural spring-fed water tanks set in a gorge in the Aravalli hills, also called the Monkey Temple.
place.history: A place of pilgrimage for centuries, the complex was later expanded with pink sandstone temples and sacred water tanks.
place.visitingInfo: Reached by a short walk through the gorge; many monkeys live here, so keep food out of sight.
place.tips: Wear sturdy footwear and avoid carrying loose food or shiny items.

place.name: Chokhi Dhani
place.description: A Rajasthani village-themed resort and cultural complex offering folk dance, puppet shows, camel rides and a traditional meal.
place.history: Created as a themed village to showcase Rajasthani folk culture, food and hospitality to visitors.
place.visitingInfo: Best visited in the evening, when performances and dinner take place.
place.tips: Go in the evening and keep time for the village-style meal.

city.name: Chennai
city.summary: Dravidian temples, colonial forts and one of the longest city beaches in the world share the Bay of Bengal.

place.name: Marina Beach
place.description: One of the longest urban beaches in the world, stretching along the Bay of Bengal with a lively promenade and street-food stalls.
place.history: Developed in the late 19th century under Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone Grant Duff, the beach has since become a cultural landmark and a hub of public life in Chennai.
place.visitingInfo: Best visited in the early morning or evening; several memorials and statues line the promenade along the beach road.
place.bestTime: November to February, and early mornings or evenings year round.
place.tips: Avoid swimming due to strong undercurrents; enjoy sunrise walks and local snacks like sundal instead.

place.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
place.description: An ancient Dravidian-style temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, recognised by its tall, colourfully sculpted gopuram (gateway tower).
place.history: The present structure dates to around the 16th century, built to replace an earlier temple destroyed by Portuguese colonists, continuing a much older Mylapore temple tradition.
place.visitingInfo: Open through the day with a break at midday; modest dress is expected and footwear must be left outside.
place.tips: Visit during the Arubathimoovar festival for a vibrant display of temple processions.

place.name: Fort St. George
place.location: Fort St. George, Chennai, Tamil Nadu
place.description: The first English fortress built in India, now housing a museum and the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly.
place.history: Built by the British East India Company in 1644, it became the nucleus around which the city of Madras (modern Chennai) grew.
place.visitingInfo: The fort museum displays colonial-era artifacts, coins, uniforms and paintings; St. Mary's Church inside is one of the oldest Anglican churches in Asia.
place.tips: Check ahead as parts of the fort may have restricted access when the legislative assembly is in session.

place.name: Government Museum
place.description: One of the oldest museums in India, with extensive galleries covering archaeology, numismatics, zoology and a celebrated bronze icon gallery.
place.history: Established in 1851, the museum complex grew over the following century to include the connected National Art Gallery in a distinctive red Indo-Saracenic building.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Fridays; the bronze gallery showcasing Chola-era sculptures is a particular highlight.
place.bestTime: Year round, ideally cooler months from November to February.
place.tips: Set aside extra time for the bronze gallery, considered one of the finest collections of South Indian bronzes.

place.name: Santhome Basilica
place.description: A striking neo-Gothic Roman Catholic basilica built over the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle, one of only three churches in the world built over an apostle's tomb.
place.history: The present structure was built by British colonists in 1896 over an earlier Portuguese-era church, marking the traditional site of St. Thomas's burial.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors of all faiths; a small museum beside the church displays relics and historical artifacts.
place.tips: Visit the adjoining museum to learn about the church's connection to the apostle's legend.

place.name: Shore Temple
place.description: A UNESCO-listed 8th-century stone temple on the Bay of Bengal shore at Mahabalipuram, among the oldest structural stone temples in South India.
place.history: Built under the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II in the early 8th century.
place.visitingInfo: About an hour's drive from Chennai along the East Coast Road; the Pancha Rathas and Arjuna's Penance can be visited on the same trip.
place.nearby: Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, Krishna's Butter Ball
place.tips: Take the scenic East Coast Road and try fresh seafood in town.

place.name: Guindy National Park
place.description: One of the smallest national parks in India and unusual for lying inside a major city, home to blackbuck, spotted deer and many birds.
place.history: The area was developed from forest land around a former governor's residence and became a national park in the 1970s.
place.visitingInfo: Trails wind through scrub forest, and the adjacent Snake Park is a popular add-on.
place.tips: Visit in the early morning, when animals are most active.

place.name: Valluvar Kottam
place.description: A memorial to the Tamil poet-saint Thiruvalluvar, shaped like a temple chariot, with a large auditorium.
place.history: Opened in 1976 to honour Thiruvalluvar, author of the Tirukkural; the chariot replicates a temple car at Thiruvarur.
place.visitingInfo: The base carries the couplets of the Tirukkural carved on stone panels.
place.tips: Read a few couplets on the panels to see how the Tirukkural is organised.

place.name: Elliot's Beach
place.description: A calmer, cleaner beach in Besant Nagar, popular for evening walks, cafes and the nearby Ashtalakshmi Temple.
place.history: Named after Edward Elliot, a British official in Madras, the beach has been a leisure spot since the colonial period.
place.visitingInfo: Quieter than Marina Beach, with food stalls and cafes nearby; swimming is not advised because of currents.
place.tips: Visit at sunrise or sunset when the light and breeze are best.

place.name: Arignar Anna Zoological Park
place.description: A large zoological park at Vandalur on the outskirts of Chennai, with open enclosures, a lion safari and many bird species.
place.history: Founded in 1855 as the Madras zoo and moved to its present Vandalur site in the 20th century.
place.visitingInfo: Battery vehicles and safari buses operate inside; plan for a long day of walking.
place.tips: Go early and carry water.

city.name: Visakhapatnam
city.summary: A coastal city framed by the Eastern Ghats, with golden beaches, hilltop parks and the gateway to Araku Valley.

place.name: RK Beach
place.location: Ramakrishna Beach Road, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh
place.description: A popular city beach and promenade along the Bay of Bengal, lined with parks, statues and the retired submarine INS Kurusura.
place.history: Named after the Ramakrishna Mission located along its shore, the beach road developed through the 20th century into the city's main public promenade.
place.visitingInfo: The promenade is best explored on foot in the evening, with several food stalls and the submarine museum nearby.
place.bestTime: October to February, evenings year round.
place.tips: Combine an evening walk here with a visit to the nearby Submarine Museum before it closes.

place.name: Kailasagiri
place.description: A hilltop park offering panoramic views over the city and coastline, reachable by road or a scenic ropeway.
place.history: Developed by the Visakhapatnam Urban Development Authority as a public recreational park on the hill overlooking the city and harbour.
place.visitingInfo: A ropeway (cable car) runs to the top; the park includes large statues of Shiva and Parvati and a toy train.
place.bestTime: November to February, or sunset any time of year.
place.tips: Take the ropeway up for sweeping views of the city, harbour and coastline in one frame.

place.name: Submarine Museum
place.description: A decommissioned Indian Navy submarine, INS Kurusura, converted into a walk-through museum, the first of its kind in Asia.
place.history: INS Kurusura served the Indian Navy for nearly three decades before being decommissioned and installed on the beach in 2002 as a public museum.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Mondays; visitors walk through the actual submarine compartments to see torpedo tubes, control rooms and crew quarters.
place.bestTime: Year round; mornings are less crowded.
place.tips: The submarine interior is narrow and can get warm, so visit in the cooler part of the day.

place.name: Araku Valley
place.location: Araku Valley, Eastern Ghats, near Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh
place.description: A scenic hill station in the Eastern Ghats known for coffee plantations, waterfalls, tribal culture and a spectacular train journey through tunnels and valleys.
place.history: Home to several tribal communities for generations, the valley's coffee cultivation and tourism infrastructure grew through the 20th century, aided by the scenic Kirandul railway line.
place.visitingInfo: Best reached by the Araku Valley train from Visakhapatnam, which passes through numerous tunnels and bridges; the Tribal Museum is a key stop.
place.nearby: Borra Caves, Tribal Museum, Ananthagiri Hills
place.tips: Book the Araku train tickets in advance and try locally grown Araku coffee.

place.name: Borra Caves
place.location: Ananthagiri Mandal, near Araku Valley, Andhra Pradesh
place.description: Ancient limestone caves with striking stalactite and stalagmite formations, among the largest cave systems in India.
place.history: Believed to be over a million years old, the caves were discovered in modern times by British geologist William King George in 1807.
place.visitingInfo: Well-lit walkways guide visitors through the cave chambers; the site is often combined with a trip to Araku Valley.
place.tips: Wear sturdy footwear since the cave floor can be slippery and uneven.

place.name: Rushikonda Beach
place.description: A golden beach below green hills, known for its clear water and water sports.
place.history: On the Bay of Bengal north of the city, it has grown into one of Vizag's main leisure and water-sports spots.
place.visitingInfo: Water sports are available in season; swim only where lifeguards permit and follow their instructions.
place.tips: Go in the morning for fewer crowds and heed the lifeguard flags.

place.name: Simhachalam Temple
place.description: A hilltop temple of Lord Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, a fine example of Kalinga and Dravidian temple architecture.
place.history: Records show the temple was patronised and expanded by several dynasties over many centuries.
place.visitingInfo: The deity is covered with sandalwood paste for most of the year and revealed on a special day, which draws very large crowds.
place.tips: Dress modestly and expect long queues around festivals.

place.name: Yarada Beach
place.description: A secluded beach enclosed by hills on three sides, with the sea on the fourth.
place.history: The beach lies near Gangavaram Port at the southern edge of the city and is reached by a scenic coastal drive.
place.visitingInfo: Quieter than the city beaches with few facilities, so carry water and snacks.
place.tips: Bring food and water, and avoid swimming in rough seas.

place.name: Thotlakonda
place.description: The ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastery complex on a hill overlooking the Bay of Bengal.
place.history: The site dates from the centuries around the start of the Common Era and was brought to light by archaeologists in the 20th century.
place.visitingInfo: The hilltop has the remains of stupas, monastic halls and cisterns, with sea views.
place.tips: Visit in the morning, as there is little shade on the hill.

place.name: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park
place.description: A large zoo set among forested hills with open enclosures and a lush backdrop.
place.history: Opened in the 1970s in the foothills of the Eastern Ghats near Kambalakonda.
place.visitingInfo: A good half-day stop; check current visiting days before you go.
place.tips: Wear comfortable shoes and carry water.

city.name: Delhi
city.summary: India's capital, layered with Mughal tombs, sultanate towers and the ceremonial avenues of Lutyens' Delhi.

place.name: India Gate
place.description: A grand sandstone war memorial arch honouring Indian soldiers who died in World War I, set amid expansive lawns.
place.history: Designed by British architect Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1931, it lists the names of over 13,000 soldiers on its walls.
place.visitingInfo: The surrounding lawns are popular for evening walks and picnics; the monument is beautifully illuminated after dark.
place.tips: Visit after sunset to see the monument lit up and enjoy the lively food-stall atmosphere on the lawns.

place.name: Red Fort
place.description: A massive red sandstone Mughal fortress that served as the main residence of Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.
place.history: Built by Emperor Shah Jahan starting in 1638 as the palace of his new capital, Shahjahanabad; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the venue for the Prime Minister's Independence Day address.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Mondays; a sound-and-light show in the evening narrates the fort's history, and the Lahori Gate market lies just outside.
place.tips: Combine your visit with Chandni Chowk market just outside for food and shopping.

place.name: Qutub Minar
place.description: The tallest brick minaret in the world, a soaring tower of intricately carved red sandstone and marble.
place.history: Construction began in 1192 under Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founder of the Delhi Sultanate, and was completed by his successors; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
place.visitingInfo: The surrounding Qutub complex includes the Iron Pillar and several other historic tombs and mosques worth exploring on the same visit.
place.tips: Explore the wider Qutub complex, not just the tower itself, to see the historic Iron Pillar and surrounding ruins.

place.name: Lotus Temple
place.description: A strikingly modern Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a blooming lotus flower, open to people of all faiths for quiet reflection.
place.history: Completed in 1986 and designed by architect Fariborz Sahba, it has won numerous architectural awards and is one of the most visited buildings in the world.
place.visitingInfo: Closed on Mondays; visitors are asked to maintain silence inside the main prayer hall regardless of their faith.
place.tips: Arrive early to avoid long entry queues, especially on weekends.

place.name: Humayun's Tomb
place.description: A grand garden tomb of red sandstone and white marble that set the architectural template later refined in the Taj Mahal.
place.history: Commissioned in 1565 by Empress Bega Begum, widow of Mughal Emperor Humayun, and completed nine years later; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
place.visitingInfo: Set within a large Persian-style char-bagh garden, the tomb complex also contains several smaller Mughal-era monuments worth exploring.
place.tips: Pair this visit with nearby Sunder Nursery, a beautifully restored heritage park.

place.name: Jama Masjid Delhi
place.description: One of the largest mosques in India, with a vast courtyard and tall minarets facing the Red Fort.
place.history: Commissioned by Shah Jahan and completed in 1656.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors outside prayer times with modest dress; the minaret climb gives views over Old Delhi.
place.tips: Cover shoulders and knees and avoid prayer times.

place.name: Akshardham Temple
place.description: A grand modern Hindu temple complex of pink sandstone and marble with exhibitions, gardens and an evening water show.
place.history: Inaugurated in 2005 and built in the traditional Indian temple style by the BAPS organisation.
place.visitingInfo: Phones, cameras and bags are not allowed inside and lockers are provided; check the current visiting days before going.
place.tips: Travel light, as electronics and large bags are not permitted.

place.name: Chandni Chowk
place.description: The famous old market street of Delhi, packed with food stalls, spice markets, havelis and temples.
place.history: Laid out in the 17th century as the main avenue of Shahjahanabad, and planned with the help of Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara.
place.visitingInfo: Best explored on foot or by cycle-rickshaw; lanes include Paranthe Wali Gali and the Khari Baoli spice market.
place.nearby: Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
place.tips: Go hungry, carry small cash and watch your belongings in the crowds.

place.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
place.description: The official residence of the President of India, a huge Lutyens-designed building at the head of Rajpath.
place.history: Designed by Edwin Lutyens and completed around 1929 as the Viceroy's House.
place.visitingInfo: Public visits to the building and the Amrit Udyan gardens run on booking, with the gardens opening to the public in late winter.
place.bestTime: February to March for the gardens, otherwise October to March.
place.tips: Book in advance and carry a government photo ID.

place.name: Lodhi Garden
place.description: A large landscaped city park scattered with 15th-century tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi dynasties.
place.history: The tombs date from the 15th and 16th centuries; the area was landscaped as a garden in the 1930s.
place.visitingInfo: Popular for morning walks, picnics and photography among the old domes.
place.tips: Visit at sunrise or late afternoon for soft light.

city.name: Mumbai
city.summary: India's financial and film capital: colonial landmarks, sea promenades, ancient island caves and a glittering waterfront.

place.name: Gateway of India
place.description: A basalt arch monument on the waterfront overlooking the Arabian Sea and the city's most famous landmark.
place.history: Built to commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary and completed in 1924.
place.visitingInfo: Ferries to Elephanta Island leave from here, and the busy promenade has the Taj Mahal Palace hotel beside it.
place.nearby: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Colaba Causeway, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
place.tips: Visit early morning or late evening and be wary of touts.

place.name: Marine Drive
place.location: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, South Mumbai, Maharashtra
place.description: A curved boulevard along the Arabian Sea, nicknamed the Queen's Necklace for its lights at night.
place.history: Reclaimed from the sea in the early 20th century and lined with Art Deco buildings from the 1930s.
place.visitingInfo: A favourite sunset spot with a long seafront walkway.
place.tips: Go at sunset and stay for the night lights; avoid high-tide days in the monsoon.

place.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
place.description: A UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic railway terminus and one of the busiest stations in India.
place.history: Designed by F. W. Stevens and completed in 1888 as Victoria Terminus.
place.visitingInfo: Best admired from outside and across the road, where the carved stonework and domes can be seen.
place.tips: Visit outside rush hour for photographs and mind your belongings.

place.name: Elephanta Caves
place.description: UNESCO-listed rock-cut cave temples on an island, dedicated to Shiva and famed for the huge Trimurti sculpture.
place.history: Carved between roughly the 5th and 8th centuries; the Portuguese named the island after an elephant statue they found.
place.visitingInfo: Reached by a ferry from the Gateway of India followed by a climb of steps; check the weekly closing day.
place.tips: Check ferry timings, as services are limited during the monsoon.

place.name: Haji Ali Dargah
place.description: A mosque and tomb on an islet in Worli Bay, reached by a causeway that is submerged at high tide.
place.history: Built in 1431 in memory of the saint Haji Ali Shah Bukhari.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors of all faiths with modest dress; check tide timings, as the path floods.
place.tips: Check tide timings before you go and dress modestly.

place.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
place.description: A large forest park inside the city, with lakes, leopards, rich birdlife and the ancient Kanheri Caves.
place.history: Established as a national park in 1969 and later renamed; the Kanheri Caves inside were carved as Buddhist monasteries.
place.visitingInfo: Nature trails, a safari and the Kanheri Caves make for a full outing within city limits.
place.tips: Start early and wear sturdy shoes.

place.name: Juhu Beach
place.description: A famous city beach known for street food such as pav bhaji and bhel puri and its lively evening crowds.
place.history: It became a popular seaside retreat for Mumbaikars and film personalities during the 20th century.
place.visitingInfo: Better for walking and food than swimming.
place.tips: Avoid swimming and pick busy, clean stalls for street food.

place.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
place.description: One of Mumbai's most visited temples, dedicated to Lord Ganesha.
place.history: First built in 1801 and rebuilt over the years.
place.visitingInfo: Queues are long on Tuesdays and festival days; modest dress is expected.
place.nearby: Worli Sea Face, Haji Ali Dargah
place.tips: Go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds.

place.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
place.description: A major museum in an Indo-Saracenic building, with art, archaeology and natural history collections, formerly the Prince of Wales Museum.
place.history: Designed by George Wittet and opened to the public in 1922.
place.visitingInfo: Galleries cover miniature painting, sculpture and decorative arts, with a garden courtyard.
place.nearby: Gateway of India, Jehangir Art Gallery
place.tips: Allow time for the miniature paintings and the garden courtyard.

place.name: Banganga Tank
place.description: An ancient sacred water tank surrounded by small temples and old houses, a calm pocket in South Mumbai.
place.history: Linked in legend to Lord Rama, the tank is believed to date back to the 12th century and was rebuilt in the 18th century.
place.visitingInfo: The nearby Walkeshwar Temple and stepped tank are quietest in the early morning.
place.tips: Visit early and respect the religious setting.

city.name: Agra
city.summary: The Mughal capital of the 16th and 17th centuries, where the Taj Mahal, a red sandstone fort and Akbar's ghost city still stand.

place.name: Taj Mahal
place.description: The ivory-white marble mausoleum on the Yamuna, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's most famous buildings.
place.history: Commissioned by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal; the main mausoleum was completed around 1643 and the full complex by about 1653.
place.visitingInfo: It is closed to general visitors on Fridays; sunrise visits are popular and tickets should be bought through official channels.
place.tips: Go at sunrise, book official tickets online and avoid Fridays.

place.name: Agra Fort
place.description: A massive red sandstone fort and UNESCO site that served as the main Mughal residence before the capital moved to Delhi.
place.history: Built by Akbar from 1565 and later enriched with marble palaces by Shah Jahan.
place.visitingInfo: Inside are the Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Jahangiri Mahal and Musamman Burj, from which the Taj Mahal is visible.
place.tips: Hire a licensed guide and look for the Taj view from Musamman Burj.

place.name: Fatehpur Sikri
place.location: Fatehpur Sikri, near Agra, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: A UNESCO-listed Mughal capital of red sandstone built by Akbar and abandoned within about fifteen years.
place.history: Founded by Akbar in 1571 and left empty a few years later, probably because of water shortage.
place.visitingInfo: The site includes the Jama Masjid, the Buland Darwaza gateway, Panch Mahal and the tomb of Salim Chishti; it lies about an hour from Agra.
place.tips: Start early and use official guides rather than unofficial touts.

place.name: Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah
place.location: Left bank of the Yamuna, Agra, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: An exquisite marble tomb with fine inlay work, often called the Baby Taj.
place.history: Built between 1622 and 1628 by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg.
place.visitingInfo: Smaller and quieter than the Taj, with delicate pietra dura inlay and carved lattice screens.
place.tips: Visit in the morning for fewer visitors and better light.

place.name: Mehtab Bagh
place.location: Across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal, Agra, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: A Mughal-style garden across the Yamuna that gives a famous view of the Taj Mahal.
place.history: Part of a line of Mughal gardens along the river, restored by the Archaeological Survey of India in the early 21st century.
place.visitingInfo: Best visited at sunset, when the Taj glows across the river.
place.tips: Come at sunset and bring a camera.

place.name: Akbar's Tomb
place.description: The grand red sandstone mausoleum of Emperor Akbar, set in a large garden with a monumental gateway.
place.history: Begun by Akbar himself and completed by his son Jahangir in the early 17th century.
place.visitingInfo: Deer roam the gardens and the four-minaret gateway is richly decorated.
place.tips: Look closely at the inlaid and carved gateway.

place.name: Jama Masjid Agra
place.location: Near Agra Fort, Agra, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: A large red sandstone and marble mosque built opposite Agra Fort.
place.history: Built in 1648 by Jahanara Begum, daughter of Shah Jahan.
place.visitingInfo: Open to visitors with modest dress and set amid a lively old market.
place.tips: Dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

place.name: Chini Ka Rauza
place.description: A 17th-century tomb decorated with glazed tilework in the Persian style.
place.history: Built around 1635 as the tomb of Afzal Khan Allami, a poet and minister under Shah Jahan.
place.visitingInfo: A quiet, little-visited site on the riverbank.
place.tips: Combine it with a visit to Itimad-ud-Daulah.

place.name: Keetham Lake
place.location: Sur Sarovar, Keetham, near Agra, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: A wetland bird sanctuary, also called Sur Sarovar, with many resident and migratory birds and a nearby bear rescue centre.
place.history: Notified as a bird sanctuary in the early 1990s and named after the poet Surdas.
place.visitingInfo: About 20 km from Agra; best for birdwatching in winter.
place.tips: Carry binoculars and go early in the morning.

place.name: Keoladeo National Park
place.description: A UNESCO World Heritage wetland near Bharatpur, famous for thousands of migratory birds.
place.history: Created as a duck-hunting reserve by the rulers of Bharatpur in the 18th century and protected as a national park in 1982.
place.visitingInfo: About 55 km from Agra; explore by bicycle or cycle-rickshaw along shaded paths.
place.tips: Hire a naturalist guide and rent a bicycle.

city.name: Varanasi
city.summary: One of the world's oldest living cities on the Ganga, where pilgrims, rituals and music flow from dawn to the evening aarti.

place.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
place.description: One of the most sacred Shiva temples in Hinduism and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.
place.history: The present temple was built in 1780 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore.
place.visitingInfo: Security is strict and phones and bags are not allowed inside; a corridor now links the temple to the Ganga ghats.
place.tips: Travel light and go early to avoid queues.

place.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
place.description: The main and liveliest ghat of Varanasi, famous for the grand Ganga Aarti held each evening.
place.history: Associated by tradition with a sacrifice by Brahma and rebuilt in the 18th century.
place.visitingInfo: Arrive early to find a place for the aarti; boat rides start here.
place.tips: Arrive an hour early for a good spot and ignore touts.

place.name: Assi Ghat
place.location: Southern end of the ghats, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: A calmer ghat at the southern end, known for sunrise gatherings, yoga, music and cultural events.
place.history: Described in texts as lying where the Assi stream meets the Ganga.
place.visitingInfo: Sunrise is the best time, when morning rituals and music programmes are held.
place.tips: Come at dawn for the best light and atmosphere.

place.name: Manikarnika Ghat
place.description: The principal cremation ghat of Varanasi, central to Hindu beliefs about liberation.
place.history: Traditionally regarded as one of the oldest and most sacred cremation grounds on the Ganga.
place.visitingInfo: Visitors should observe respectfully from a distance and avoid photographing rituals.
place.tips: Do not photograph funerals and ignore anyone demanding money.

place.name: Sarnath
place.description: The place where the Buddha gave his first teaching, with monastery ruins, stupas and a museum.
place.history: After enlightenment at Bodh Gaya the Buddha taught here; the emperor Ashoka later raised monuments at the site.
place.visitingInfo: The archaeological park and the Sarnath Museum, home of the Ashoka Lion Capital, are the main stops; check the museum's weekly closing day.
place.tips: Visit the museum to see the Lion Capital, India's national emblem.

place.name: Dhamek Stupa
place.description: A massive cylindrical stupa marking the spot where the Buddha is believed to have given his first sermon.
place.history: Built around the 5th or 6th century CE over an earlier Mauryan structure.
place.visitingInfo: The lower part is covered in fine geometric and floral carvings, set in a peaceful park.
place.tips: Combine with the Sarnath Museum in the same visit.

place.name: Ramnagar Fort
place.location: Ramnagar, across the Ganga from Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
place.description: An 18th-century fort and palace on the eastern bank of the Ganga, long the residence of the Maharaja of Benares.
place.history: Built in 1750 by Raja Balwant Singh of Kashi.
place.visitingInfo: A museum inside displays vintage cars, costumes and weapons; it can be reached by boat or bridge.
place.tips: Cross the river by boat for a fine view of the ghats.

place.name: Durga Temple Varanasi
place.description: A red ochre temple dedicated to Goddess Durga, built in the Nagara style and often called the Monkey Temple.
place.history: Built in the 18th century, according to tradition by a Bengali queen.
place.visitingInfo: Stands beside the rectangular Durga Kund pond and is especially busy during Navratri.
place.nearby: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple, Banaras Hindu University
place.tips: Visit during Navratri to see the biggest celebrations.

place.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
place.description: A well-known Hanuman temple, famous for a week-long classical music festival each spring.
place.history: Founded in the early 20th century by Madan Mohan Malaviya.
place.visitingInfo: Open from early morning and crowded on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
place.tips: Avoid Tuesdays and Saturdays if you prefer smaller crowds.

place.name: Banaras Hindu University
place.description: One of Asia's largest residential universities, with a green campus, the Bharat Kala Bhavan museum and the New Vishwanath Temple.
place.history: Founded in 1916 by Madan Mohan Malaviya.
place.visitingInfo: The campus is open to visitors; the New Vishwanath Temple and the museum are the main draws.
place.tips: Visit on a weekday morning and respect campus rules.

city.name: Kolkata
city.summary: The former capital of British India: grand colonial buildings, riverside temples, literature, sweets and a lively intellectual culture.

place.name: Victoria Memorial
place.description: A white marble museum and monument set in landscaped gardens, dedicated to Queen Victoria.
place.history: Built between 1906 and 1921 to a design by William Emerson.
place.visitingInfo: Galleries cover the city's colonial history, and the gardens and an evening light-and-sound show are popular; check the weekly closing day.
place.nearby: St. Paul's Cathedral, Maidan, Indian Museum
place.tips: Visit in the evening for the gardens and illuminated building.

place.name: Howrah Bridge
place.location: Over the Hooghly, Kolkata, West Bengal
place.description: A famous steel cantilever bridge, among the busiest of its type in the world, linking Kolkata and Howrah.
place.history: Opened in 1943 and renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965.
place.visitingInfo: Walk across for river views and look down at the Mullick Ghat flower market.
place.nearby: Mullick Ghat Flower Market, Howrah Station
place.tips: Cross at sunrise or sunset and take care in the traffic.

place.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
place.description: A major Kali temple on the Hooghly, closely linked with the saint Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
place.history: Built in 1855 by Rani Rashmoni.
place.visitingInfo: The large complex includes twelve Shiva temples and riverside steps.
place.tips: Go early in the morning; footwear is not allowed in the temple.

place.name: Belur Math
place.description: Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, with a temple blending Hindu, Islamic and Christian architectural motifs on the Hooghly.
place.history: Established by Swami Vivekananda in the late 19th century; the main temple was completed in 1938.
place.visitingInfo: A peaceful riverside campus; ferries connect it with Dakshineswar.
place.tips: Visit in the evening for aarti and dress modestly.

place.name: Indian Museum
place.description: The oldest and one of the largest museums in India, with galleries of art, archaeology, anthropology, geology and zoology.
place.history: Founded in 1814 by the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
place.visitingInfo: Highlights include the Egyptian mummy and the Bharhut stupa gallery; check the weekly closing day.
place.tips: Allow plenty of time, as the collections are vast.

place.name: St. Paul's Cathedral
place.description: An Anglican cathedral in Indo-Gothic style with a tall tower and stained glass.
place.history: Consecrated in 1847 to a design by Major William Nairn Forbes.
place.visitingInfo: A calm interior with fine glass; services are held on Sundays.
place.tips: Visit around Christmas to see the cathedral decorated.

place.name: Marble Palace
place.location: Muktaram Babu Street, Kolkata, West Bengal
place.description: A 19th-century mansion filled with marble floors, statues, chandeliers and European paintings.
place.history: Built in 1835 by the wealthy merchant Raja Rajendra Mullick.
place.visitingInfo: Entry has usually required prior permission, so check current rules before visiting.
place.tips: Arrange permission in advance and dress modestly.

place.name: Eden Gardens
place.description: One of the most famous cricket stadiums in the world, with a unique atmosphere on match days.
place.history: Established in 1864 and named after the Eden sisters, relatives of a British governor-general.
place.visitingInfo: Best experienced during a match; tickets are needed.
place.tips: Book tickets early and arrive early to enter.

place.name: Science City
place.description: One of the largest science centres in South Asia, with interactive exhibits, a space theatre and an evolution park.
place.history: Opened in the 1990s as a centre for popular science education.
place.visitingInfo: A full-day outing for families, with galleries and shows for children.
place.tips: Pre-book show tickets to save time.

place.name: Kalighat Temple
place.description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas and an important pilgrimage site for devotees of Kali.
place.history: The present temple structure was completed in the early 19th century.
place.visitingInfo: Large crowds and queues are normal; modest dress is expected.
place.tips: Go early in the morning to avoid long queues.

city.name: Goa
city.summary: Sun, sand and a layered Indo-Portuguese heritage: UNESCO churches, hilltop forts, spice-scented villages and a long Arabian Sea coast.

place.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
place.description: A UNESCO-listed church that holds the relics of St Francis Xavier.
place.history: Built between 1594 and 1605 during Portuguese rule.
place.visitingInfo: Part of the Old Goa churches complex; modest dress is expected.
place.nearby: Se Cathedral, Church of St Francis of Assisi
place.tips: Cover shoulders and knees and visit with Se Cathedral in the same morning.

place.name: Fort Aguada
place.description: A 17th-century Portuguese fort overlooking the Arabian Sea, with an old lighthouse.
place.history: Built in 1612 to guard the entrance of the Mandovi river against Dutch and Maratha ships.
place.visitingInfo: The fort takes its name from the Portuguese word for water, after its freshwater spring; the lighthouse is among the oldest in Asia.
place.tips: Visit at sunset for the best light over the sea.

place.name: Baga Beach
place.description: A lively North Goa beach famed for water sports, beach shacks and nightlife.
place.history: Once a quiet fishing village, it grew into a major tourist hub from the 1970s onward.
place.visitingInfo: Water sports and shacks line the sand; swim only in marked areas.
place.tips: Check flag warnings and use licensed water-sport operators.

place.name: Calangute Beach
place.description: The largest beach in North Goa, often called the Queen of Beaches.
place.history: It rose to popularity as a tourist destination in the late 20th century.
place.visitingInfo: Crowded in peak season, with shacks, markets and water sports.
place.tips: Go in the morning for a quieter experience.

place.name: Anjuna Beach
place.description: A rocky, laid-back beach known for its weekly flea market and sunset spots.
place.history: It became known during the hippie era of the 1960s.
place.visitingInfo: The famous flea market is held once a week, usually on Wednesdays.
place.tips: Reach the flea market early and bargain politely.

place.name: Dudhsagar Falls
place.description: A tall four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi river, among the tallest in India, set in forest at the Goa and Karnataka border.
place.history: Its name means Sea of Milk, from the white spray that cascades down the cliff.
place.visitingInfo: Usually reached by a jeep safari through the forest; access can be restricted during the monsoon.
place.nearby: Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, Tambdi Surla Temple
place.tips: Check access conditions and wear shoes with good grip.

place.name: Se Cathedral
place.description: One of the largest churches in Asia, dedicated to St Catherine of Alexandria and known for its Golden Bell.
place.history: Construction began in the 16th century and took many decades to complete.
place.visitingInfo: Part of the UNESCO-listed Old Goa complex.
place.nearby: Basilica of Bom Jesus, Church of St Francis of Assisi
place.tips: Visit together with Bom Jesus in one trip.

place.name: Chapora Fort
place.description: A ruined hilltop fort with sweeping views over Vagator beach and the Chapora river.
place.history: Built by the Adil Shahi sultans of Bijapur and rebuilt by the Portuguese in the early 17th century.
place.visitingInfo: A short uphill walk leads to ruined walls and viewpoints.
place.tips: Go in late afternoon for sunset and wear shoes with grip.

place.name: Palolem Beach
place.description: A crescent-shaped, calmer beach in South Goa lined with palm trees and known for kayaking.
place.history: A fishing area that has become a quieter alternative to the busy northern beaches.
place.visitingInfo: Kayaking and dolphin-spotting trips are popular.
place.nearby: Agonda Beach, Cabo de Rama Fort
place.tips: Try a sunrise kayak ride.

place.name: Fontainhas
place.description: A charming Latin Quarter of Panaji with narrow lanes, colourful Portuguese-style houses and the Chapel of St Sebastian.
place.history: Developed in the 19th century as a residential area of Portuguese-era Goa.
place.visitingInfo: Best explored on foot, with art galleries and cafes in the lanes.
place.tips: Walk in the morning and look for the traditional tile nameplates.
